house-home.previewSummary: Known homes, unfamiliar houses and impossible mansions repeatedly organise belonging, memory, privacy, intrusion and discovery.

recurringFunctions.name: Belonging made architectural
recurringFunctions.summary: Family, partners, children, animals, food and care repeatedly organise themselves through kitchens, bedrooms, gardens and shared interiors. The house may externalise the question of who and what belongs here.

recurringFunctions.name: Porous boundaries and intrusion
recurringFunctions.summary: Uninvited people, volatile inhabitants, hostile forces and displaced possessions repeatedly disturb domestic space. The house may stage the work of establishing psychological and relational boundaries.

recurringFunctions.name: More rooms than consciousness expects
recurringFunctions.summary: Large and unfamiliar houses disclose extra rooms, levels, corridors and concealed life. Expanding architecture may image unrealised capacities, memories or complexes becoming available for exploration.

interpretiveLenses.name: Jungian: psyche / personality
interpretiveLenses.summary: A house can be amplified as an image of psychic structure: different levels and rooms may suggest differentiated areas of experience, but this reading must be tested against each dream.
interpretiveLenses.caveat: The house is the psyche is an amplification, not a translation key.

interpretiveLenses.name: Jungian: Self and totality
interpretiveLenses.summary: Impossible scale or a building that behaves as a whole may intimate a psychic totality larger than the conscious ego; haunted and many-roomed houses are stronger candidates than ordinary kitchens.

interpretiveLenses.name: Autobiographical and attachment
interpretiveLenses.summary: Childhood and present houses can combine episodic memory, safety, proximity and caregiving without functioning as disguised symbols.

house-home.possibleLesson: Belonging may be something continually defended, reorganised and made habitable rather than something permanently secured.
house-home.reflectionPrompt: Which house feels most yours, and what is happening to belonging there: shelter, crowding, discovery, inheritance, intrusion, repair or expansion?

water.previewSummary: Water repeatedly becomes a medium of crossing, immersion, play, overwhelm, rescue and renewed embodiment rather than carrying one fixed meaning.

recurringFunctions.name: Crossing between worlds
recurringFunctions.summary: Shores, rivers, boats and islands repeatedly make water the material boundary between a present position and another possible world.

recurringFunctions.name: Overwhelm and contested control
recurringFunctions.summary: Floods, currents, storms, sinking and uncontrolled water recur when plans or containers fail, giving spatial form to intensity that exceeds ordinary regulation.

recurringFunctions.name: Play, immersion and restoration
recurringFunctions.summary: A contrasting group of dreams enters water bodily, rediscovers play or encounters beauty and renewal, suggesting that immersion can sometimes restore contact with vitality.

interpretiveLenses.name: Jungian: unconscious depth
interpretiveLenses.summary: Water may image psychic material not fully available to conscious control, especially where the dream moves beneath surfaces or into unknown depth.
interpretiveLenses.caveat: Water is not automatically emotion or the unconscious; form, movement, companions and agency matter.

interpretiveLenses.name: Liminal passage
interpretiveLenses.summary: Rivers and shores create thresholds: the dreamer must cross, enter or negotiate a boundary between states rather than merely observe it.

interpretiveLenses.name: Embodied memory
interpretiveLenses.summary: Coasts, swimming, weather and holidays may also draw directly on sensory memory and waking concerns.

water.possibleLesson: The recurring question may be how to enter emotional or unconscious depth without losing agency, and how responsibility for others changes that immersion.
water.reflectionPrompt: Is the water asking you to cross, surrender, play, rescue, contain, survive, or simply remember a real landscape and bodily feeling?

cat.previewSummary: Cats repeatedly gather a tension between cherished vulnerability and irreducible autonomy: close enough to require care, but never wholly manageable.

recurringFunctions.name: Vulnerable life calling forth protection
recurringFunctions.summary: Cats repeatedly face vehicles, hostile figures, injury, disappearance, fire or unsafe boundaries, prompting urgent rescue and practical care.

recurringFunctions.name: Instinct that exceeds domestication
recurringFunctions.summary: Cats become lion-like, elusive, speaking, resistant or unexpectedly capable, repeatedly exceeding the passive role assigned to a pet.

interpretiveLenses.name: Jungian: instinctive companion
interpretiveLenses.summary: The cat can mediate between domestic consciousness and a more self-directed instinctive life: close to the household, but never wholly possessed by it.

interpretiveLenses.name: Care ethics
interpretiveLenses.summary: The recurring question may be how responsibility remains responsive to the preferences of a dependent but agentic other.

interpretiveLenses.name: Literal attachment
interpretiveLenses.summary: Real interspecies attachment can explain vigilance, grief and caregiving without requiring archetypal interpretation.

cat.possibleLesson: Protection may need to become attentive partnership: caring intensely without erasing the autonomy of the life being cared for.
cat.reflectionPrompt: Is the cat asking for rescue, food, space, trust, attention, or recognition that its instinct knows something your conscious plan does not?

dog.previewSummary: Dogs oscillate between companion and sentinel, repeatedly testing loyalty, belonging, warning, guarding and the reliability of protective instinct.

recurringFunctions.name: Companionship woven into family life
recurringFunctions.summary: Known dogs repeatedly appear with family, fields, houses and other animals as energetic members of a shared relational world.

recurringFunctions.name: Guarding, warning and misjudged threat
recurringFunctions.summary: Dogs bark, guard thresholds, chase vulnerable figures or appear threatening; other dreams expose apparent protection as ineffective or mistaken.

interpretiveLenses.name: Jungian: instinctive guardian
interpretiveLenses.summary: The dog can amplify protective instinct at the edge of consciousness, alerting the ego to what approaches the household or group.

interpretiveLenses.name: Threat detection
interpretiveLenses.summary: Barking, chasing and guarding can dramatise rapid judgements about safety and uncertainty without requiring symbolic translation.

interpretiveLenses.name: Literal attachment
interpretiveLenses.summary: Known dogs carry real affection, memory and grief that should precede symbolic amplification.

dog.possibleLesson: The pattern may ask which protective instincts deserve trust, which need moderation, and when apparent guardianship is only performance.
dog.reflectionPrompt: Is this dog accompanying, playing, resting, warning, guarding, chasing, or pretending to protect, and does your body trust its judgement?
